title: Σ
content:
Σ, σ, final ς, σίγμα, τό, indecl.,

sigma, the eighteenth letter. As a numeral, σʹ = 200, σ͵ = 200,000.

title: σαβαχθανεί
content:
† σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.c., WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי),

sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 (Ps 21 (22):2, Heb. עֲוַבְתָּנִי).†

title: σαβαώθ
content:
† σαβαώθ indecl., [in LXX for צְבָאוֺת, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase יהוה צי is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; v. DB, iii, 137 f.) ;]

Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (v. DB, l.c.): Ro 9:29 (LXX), Ja 5:4.†

title: σαββατισμός
content:
*† σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Ex 16:30, al.),

a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaph., as in Mishna (Zorell, s.v.), He 4:9.†

title: σάββατον
content:
† σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά [in LXX for שַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּתוֹן ;]

1. the seventh day of the week, the sabbath
(a) the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: Mt 12:8, Mk 2:27, Lk 6:5, al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, Ex 20:8, al., usually τῶν σ., v. infr.), Lk 13:16 14:5; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, Ac 1:12 (cf. Mt 24:20); dat., of time (τῷ) σ., Lk 6:9 14:1; ἐν (τῷ) σ., Mt 12:2, Lk 6:7, Jo 5:16, al.; acc., of duration, τὸ σ., Lk 23:56; κατὰ πᾶν σ., Ac 13:27 15:21 18:4; pl., σ. τρία, Ac 17:2 R, txt. (but v. infr.);
(b) as most freq. in LXX (v. Swete, Mk., 17; Thackeray, Gr., 35) the pl. form, τὰ σ. (v. supr. on the Aram. form. There is also an analogy in the names of other festivals, τ. ἐγκαίνια, ἄζυμα, etc.): Mt 28:1, Col 2:16; ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν σ. (Ex 20:8, al.), Lk 4:16, Ac 13:14 16:13; dat. pl. (in LXX -τοις, but I Mac 2:38 as in NT) by metaplasmus (Bl., § 9, 3), σάββασι, Mt 12:1, 5, 10–12 Mk 1:21 2:23 3:2, 4, Lk 4:31 6:2.
2. seven days, a week;
(a) the sing. form: πρώτη σαββάτσυ, Mk 16:9; δὶς τοῦ σ. (Bl., § 35, 4; 36, 13), Lk 18:12; κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου, I Co 16:2; pl., σ. τρία, Ac 17:2 R, mg. (but v. supr.);
(b) the pl. form: ἡ μία τῶν σ. (where the gen. = μετὰ τά; Soph., Lex., 43a), Mt 28:1, Mk 16:2, Lk 24:1, Jo 20:1, 19, Ac 20:7

title: σαγήνη
content:
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶם ;]

a drag-net, seine: Mt 13:47.†
SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (q.v.), δίκτυον

title: Σαδδουκαῖος
content:
Σαδδουκαῖος, -ου, ὁ (< Heb. צָדוֹק, II Ki 15:24, al.),

a Sadducee (cf. Swete, Mk., 277): Mt 3:7 16:1, 6, 11, 12 22:23, 34, Mk 12:18, Lk 20:27, Ac 4:1 5:17 23:6–8.†

title: Σαδώκ
content:
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, v. supr., s.v. Σαδδουκαῖος)

Sadoc, Zadok: Mt 1:14.†

title: σαίνω
content:
* σαίνω

1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn.
2. Metaph., of persons, c. acc., to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., I Th 3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, v. ICC, and M, Th., in l.).†

title: σάκκος
content:
σάκκος also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ (cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX),

1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Re 6:12.
2. Anything made of sackcloth;
(a) a sack (Ge 42:25, al.);
(b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13, Re 11:3.†

title: Σαλά
content:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שָׁלַח),

Sala, Shalah: Lk 3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, q.v.), ib. 35.†

title: Σαλαθιήλ
content:
Σαλαθιήλ, ὁ

indecl. (Heb. שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל),
Salathiel: Mt 1:12, Lk 3:27.†

title: Σαλαμίς
content:
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνος, ἡ

Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Ac 13:5.†

title: Σαλείμ
content:
Σαλείμ, τό indecl.,

Salim: Jo 3:23 (v. Westc., in l.; DB, iii, 354).†

title: σαλεύω
content:
σαλεύω (< σάλος), [in LXX for מוּט, נוּעַ, etc. ;]

prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mt 11:7, Lk 7:24; a house, Lk 6:48, Ac 4:31 16:26; the earth, He 12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mt 24:29, Mk 13:25, Lk 21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Lk 6:38. Metaph.,
(a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., He 12:27;
(b) c. acc pers., to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: Ac 2:25 (LXX);
(c) to unsettle or drive away: pass., seq. ἀπὸ τ. νοός, II Th 2:2;
(d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, Ac 17:13.†

title: Σαλήμ
content:
Σαλήμ, ἡ (Heb. שָׁלֵם Ge 14:18),

Salem: He 7:1, 2 (LXX).†

title: Σαλμών
content:
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן),

Salmon: Mt 1:4, 5, Lk 3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†

title: Σαλμώνη
content:
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ

Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Ac 27:7.†

title: σάλος
content:
σάλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;]

in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Lk 21:25.†

title: σάλπιγξ
content:
σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;]

a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: I Co 14:8, He 12:19, Re 1:10 4:1 8:2, 6, 13 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mt 24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, I Th 4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., I Co 15:52.†

title: σαλπίζω
content:
σαλπίζω [in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;]

to sound a trumpet: Re 8:6 ff. 9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaph., Mt 6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: I Co 15:52.†

title: σαλπιστής
content:
* σαλπιστής (so Inscr. and late writers for Att. σαλπιγκτής), -οῦ, ὁ,

a trumpeter: Re 18:22.†

title: Σαλώμη
content:
Σαλώμη, -ης, ἡ (< Heb. שָׁלוֹם),

Salome: Mk 15:40 16:1.†

title: Σαλωμών
content: Σαλωμών, v.s. Σολομών.

title: Σαμάρεια
content: Σαμάρεια, v.s. Σαμαρία.

title: Σαμαρείτης
content:
Σαμαρείτης (-ίτης, Τ; v. WH, App., 154; Bl., § 3, 4), -ου, ό,

a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (v.s. Σαμαρία): Mt 10:5, Lk 9:52 10:33 17:16, Jo 4:9, 39, 40, Ac 8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jo 8:48.†

title: Σαμαρεῖτις
content:
Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, v. supr.), -ιδος, ἡ

1. in FlJ (B.J., I, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria.
2. a Samaritan woman: Jo 4:9.†

title: Σαμαρία
content:
Σαμαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ (Heb. שֹׁמְרוֹן; Aram. שָׁמְרַיִן),

Samaria;
(a) the city: Ac 8:5 (and perhaps also 9, 14);
(b) the region: Lk 17:11, Jo 4:4, 5, 7, Ac 1:8 8:1 (and perhaps also 8:9, 14) 9:31 15:3.†

title: Σαμοθρᾴκη
content:
Σαμοθρᾴκη (-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ

Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: Ac 16:11.†

title: Σάμος
content:
Σάμος, -ου, ἡ

Samos, an island in the Ægean: Ac 20:15.†

title: Σαμουήλ
content:
Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל),

Samuel (I Ki 1:20, al.): Ac 3:24 13:20, He 11:32.†

title: Σαμψών
content:
Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן),

Samson (Jg 13 ff.): He 11:32.†

title: σανδάλιον
content:
σανδάλιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Jos 9:5, Is 20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, q.v.), Jth 10:4 16:9 * ;]

a sandal: Mk 6:9, Ac 12:8.†

title: σανίς
content:
σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX: Ca 8:9, Ez 27:5 (לוּחַ) * ;]

a board, plank: Ac 27:44

title: Σαούλ
content:
Σαούλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל)

Saul;
(a) the King of Israel: Ac 13:21;
(b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): Ac 9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14.†

title: σαπρός
content:
** σαπρός, -ά -όν [in Sm.: Le 27:14, 33 * ;]

rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opp. to ἀγαθός, καλός), Mt 7:17, 18 12:33 Lk 6:43; of fish, Mt 13:48.
Metaph., in moral sense: λόγος σ., Eph 4:29. "In Hellenistic … it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.†

title: Σαπφείρα
content:
Σαπφείρα, -ης (v. B1., § 3, 4), ἡ (< Aram. שַׁפִּירָא)

Sapphira: Ac 5:1.†

title: σάπφειρος
content:
† σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for סַפִּיר ;]

sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Re 21:19.†

title: σαργάνη
content:
* σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ

1. a plaited rope (Æsch.).
2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: II Co 11:33.†

title: Σάρδεις
content:
Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ

Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Re 1:11 3:1, 4.†

title: σάρδινος
content:
† σάρδινος, -ου, ὁ

= σάρδιον (q.v.), Re 4:3, Rec.†

title: σάρδιον
content:
σάρδιον, -ον, τό [in LXX for אֹדֶם, Ex 28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;]

the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Re 4:3 21:20.†

title: σαρδόνυξ
content:
* σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ (< σάρδιον, ὄνυξ),

sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Re 21:20.†

title: Σάρεπτα
content:
Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת),

Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Lk 4:26.†

title: σαρκικός
content:
* σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (< σάρξ) (v.l. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7)

= Lat. carnalis, i.e.
(a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Ro 15:27, I Co 9:11;
(b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, I Pe., 133): I Co 3:3, II Co 1:12 10:4, I Pe 2:11.†
SYN.: σάρκινος (q.v.), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ lxxi, lxxii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Ro 7:14

title: σάρκινος
content:
σάρκινος, -η, -ον (< σάρξ), [in LXX: II Ch 32:8, Ez 11:19 36:26 (בָּשָׂר), Es 4:17, Pr 24:23 (29:27) * ;]

= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; v. Tr., Syn., § lxxii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., v. MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Ro 7:14, I Co 3:1, II Co 3:3, He 7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except II Co, l.c., but the evidence is decisive against it.)†
SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v

title: σάρξ
content:
σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]

flesh;
1. as in cl. generally,
(a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: I Co 15:39, II Co 12:7, Ga 6:13, al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, I Co 5:50; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, Lk 24:39; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), Re 17:16 19:18; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. c. (cf. κατεσθίειν, IV Ki 9:36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, freq. in l.); metaph., Ja 5:3; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, Jo 6:52–56;
(b) Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: Ac 2:26 (LXX), 31, II Co 12:7, Ga 4:14, Eph 5:29; μία σ., Mk 10:8; εἰς σ. μίαν (Ge 2:24), Mt 19:5, Mk 10:8, I Co 6:16, Eph 5:31; hence, of the material as opp. to the immaterial part of man (cf. Lft., Notes, 88): opp. to πνεῦμα, I Co 5:5, II Co 7:1, Col 2:5, I Pe 3:18, 4:6; to ψύχη, Ac 2:31, Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Ro 7:5, Ga 2:20, Phl 1:22, 24 I Pe 4:2; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, He 5:7; of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Ga 6:12, 13, Phl 3:3, 4.
2. As in Heb. idiom,
(a) of a living creature: πᾶσα σ. (Heb. כָּל־בָּשָׂר; cf. Bl., § 47, 9), Mt 24:22, Mk 13:20, I Pe 1:24; esp. of man and his mortality (Ps 55 (56):5, Si 28:5, al.), Jo 1:14; πᾶσα σ. (v. supr.), Lk 3:6, Jo 17:2, Ac 2:17, ἐν σ., I Jo 4:2, I Ti 3:16;
(b) of natural origin and relationship (Ge 2:24, Is 58:7, al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., Ro 9:8; κατὰ σάρκα, ib. 3, 5, I Co 10:18, Ga 4:23, 29; ἡ σ. μου, Ro 11:14 (cf. Jg 9:2, II Ki 5:1, al.).
3. Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.),
(a) without any ethical disparagement: Ro 7:18 13:14; opp. to πνεῦμα, Mt 26:41, Mk 14:38; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., Jo 1:13; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., I Jo 2:16; pl., II Pe 2:18; παθεῖν σαρκί, I Pe 4:1;
(b) in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opp. to νοῦς, Ro 7:25; to πνεῦμα, Ro 8:4–9, 12, 13, Ga 5:16, 17, 19 6:8 (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844 ff.).

title: Σαρούχ
content: Σαρούχ, v.s. Σερούχ.

title: σαρόω
content:
* σαρόω, -ῶ

late form of σαίρω,
to sweep: c. acc, Lk 15:8; pass., Mt 12:44, Lk 11:25.†

title: Σάρρα
content:
Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, Ge 17:15),

Sarah: Ro 4:19 9:9, He 11:11, I Pe 3:6.†

title: Σάρων
content:
Σάρων, -ωνος (acc -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן),

the plain of Sharon: Ac 9:35.†

title: Σατανᾶς
content:
Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ (so also Sir 21:30, but in III Ki 11:14, σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό,

Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. c.): Mt 4:10 12:26, Mk 1:13 3:23, 26 4:15, Lk 10:18 11:18 13:16 22:3, 31, Jo 13:27, Ac 5:3 26:18, Ro 16:20, I Co 5:5 7:5, II Co 2:11 11:14, I Th 2:18, II Th 2:9, I Ti 1:20 5:15, Re 2:9, 13, 24 3:9 12:9 20:2, 7; addressed in person of Peter, Mt 16:23 Mk 8:33; ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, II Co 12:7.†

title: σάτον
content:
† σάτον, -ου, τό (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Hg 2:17 (16) * ;]

a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mt 13:33, Lk 13:21.†

title: Σαῦλος
content:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, q.v.),

Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: Ac 7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8, 11, 22, 24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1, 2, 7, 9.†

title: σβέννυμι
content:
σβέννυμι [in LXX chiefly for כּבה ;]

of fire or things on fire, to quench: c. acc, Mt 12:20, Eph 6:16, He 11:34; pass., Mt 25:8, Mk 9:[44, 46], 48, Metaph. (cf. Ca 8:7, IV Mac 16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, I Th 5:19.†

title: σεαυτοῦ
content:
σεαυτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ (in NT not contracted, σαυτοῦ, as in Att..), reflex. prop. of 2nd pers. sing., used only in gen., dat. and acc.

(of, to) thyself: Mt 4:6, Jo 8:13, I Ti 4:16, al. (In Hellenistic, the pl. is ἑαυτῶν (q.v.), not ὑμῶν αὐτῶν as in Attic, v. Bl., § 13, 1.) †

title: σεβάζομαι
content:
** σεβάζομαι (< σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: Ho 10:5 * ;]

1. to fear (Hom).
2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Ro 1:25

title: σέβασμα
content:
** σέβασμα, -τος, τό (< σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wi 14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;]

an object of worship: Ac 17:23, II Th 2:4.†

title: σεβαστός
content:
* σεβαστός, -ή, -όν (σεβάζομαι)

1. reverend, august.
2. In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name;
(a) ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: Ac 25:21, 25;
(b) Augustan: σπείρα σ., Ac 27:1 (See further, Deiss., BS, 218.) †

title: σέβω
content:
σέβω [in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, Jos 4:24, al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. IV Mac 5:24 ;]

to worship: c. acc. pers., Mt 15:9, Mk 7:7, Ac 18:13 19:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, Ac 16:14 18:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, Ac 13:43, 50 17:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†

title: σειρά
content:
σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: Jg 16:13, 14, 19 (מַחְלָפוֺת), Pr 5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;]

1.
(a) a cord;
(b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.c.): σειραὶ ζόφου, II Pe 2:4, Rec., R, mg. (v.s. σειρός).
2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. c.).†

title: σειρός
content:
* σειρός (σιρός, T), -οῦ, ὁ (Rec., R, mg., σειρά, q.v.), = cl. σιρός,

a pit for the storage of grain: σειροὶ ζόφου, II Pe 2:4, WH, R., txt. (but v. Mayor, in l.; Field, Notes, 241).†

title: σεισμός
content:
σεισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ ;]

a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: Mt 8:24; esp. an earthquake: Mt 24:7 27:54 28:2, Mk 13:8, Lk 21:11, Ac 16:26, Re 6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18.†

title: σείω
content:
σείω [in LXX chiefly for רעשׁ ;]

to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, He 12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Mt 27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Re 6:13. Metaph., to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Mt 21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†

title: Σέκουνδος
content:
Σέκουνδος (Rec. Σεκοῦνδος), -ου, ὁ

(Lat.), Secundus: Ac 20:4.†

title: Σελευκία
content:
Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια),

Seleucia, a city of Syria: Ac 13:4.†

title: σελήνη
content:
σελήνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ (Ge 37:9, al.), also for לְבָנָה; (Ca 6:9 (10), Is 24:23א, 30:26) ;]

the moon: Mt 24:29, Mk 13:24, Lk 21:25, Ac 2:20 (LXX), I Co 15:41, Re 6:12 8:12 12:1 21:23.†

title: σεληνιάζω
content:
*† σεληνιάζω (< σελήνη), act, in Manetho (Carm., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι,

to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Mt 4:24 17:15.†

title: Σεμεείν
content:
Σεμεείν (Rec. Σεμεΐ), ὁ, indecl.,

Semein: Lk 3:26.†

title: σεμίδαλις
content:
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;]

fine wheaten flour: Re 18:13.†

title: σεμνός
content:
σεμνός, -ή, -όν (< σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pr 6:8 8:6 15:26(נָגִיד,נֹעַם), II Mac 6:11, 6:28 8:15, IV Mac 5:36 7:15 17:5 * ;]

1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings.
2. grave, serious; of persons: I Ti 3:8, 11, Tit 2:2; of things: Phl 4:8 (v. Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†

title: σεμνότης
content:
** σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (< σεμνός), [in LXX: II Mac 3:12 * ;]

gravity: I Ti 2:2 3:4 (Vg. castitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, s.v.), Tit 2:7.†

title: Σέργιος
content:
Σέργιος, -ου, ὁ

Sergius, surnamed Paulus: Ac 13:7.†

title: Σερούχ
content:
Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג),

Serug: Lk 3:35.†

title: Σήθ
content:
Σήθ, ὁ (Heb. שֵׁת),

indecl.,
Seth (Ge 4:25): Lk 3:38.†

title: Σήμ
content:
Σήμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֵׁם),

Shem: Lk 3:36.†

title: σημαίνω
content:
σημαίνω (< σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע, etc. ;]

to give a sign, signify, indicate: c. acc. rei, Ac 25:27, Re 1:1 (cf. MM, xxii); c. acc. et inf., Ac 11:28; seq. quæst. indir., Jo 12:33 18:32 21:19.†

title: σημεῖον
content:
σημεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for אוֹת ;]

a sign, mark, token;
(a) of that which distinguishes a person or thing from others: Mt 26:48, Lk 2:12, II Th 3:17 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 1532); seq. gen. epexeg., Ro 4:11; c. gen. obj., Mt 24:8, 30, II Co 12:12; c. gen. subj., Mt 16:3;
(b) a sign of warning or admonition: Mt 12:39 16:4, Lk 2:34 11:29, 30, I Co 14:22;
(c) a sign portending future events (Soph., Plat. al.): Mk 13:4, Lk 21:7, 11, 25, Ac 2:19, Re 12:1, 3 15:1;
(d) of miracles and wonders (MM, xxii), regarded as signs of a divine authority: Mt 12:38, 39 16:1, 4, Mk 8:11, 12 Lk 11:16, 29 23:8, Jo 2:11, 18, 23 4:54 6:30 10:41 12:18, Ac 4:16, 22; pl., Mk 16:[17, 20], Jo 2:11, 23 3:2 6:2, 14, 26 7:31 9:16 11:47 12:37 20:30, Ac 8:6, I Co 1:22 (Lft., Notes, 162); the same ascribed to false teachers and demons: Mt 24:24, Mk 13:22, II Th 2:9, Re 13:13, 14 16:14 19:20; σ. καὶ τέρατα (τ. καὶ σ.; cf. Tr., Syn., § xci), Mt 24:24, Mk 13:22, Jo 4:48, Ac 2:19, 43 4:30 5:12 6:8 7:36 14:3 15:12, Ro 15:19, II Th 2:9; id. seq. καὶ δυνάμεις, II Co 12:12, He 2:4; σ. καὶ δυνάμεις, Ac 8:13; δ. καὶ τ. καὶ σ., Ac 2:22; σ. διδόναι, Mt 24:24, Mk 13:22.†

title: σημειόω
content:
σημειόω, -ῶ (< σημεῖον), [in LXX: Ps 4:6 (נשׂא)* ;]

to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: II Th 3:14 (freq. in π.; v. ICC, M, Th., in l.).†

title: σήμερον
content:
σήμερον (Att.. τήμερον), adv., [in LXX for הַיּוֺם ;]

to-day: Mt 6:11, Lk 4:21, Ac 4:9, al.; opp. to αὔριον, Mt 6:30, Lk 12:28, Ja 4:13; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, He 13:8; ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, Ac 20:26; ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, Ro 11:8, II Co 3:14; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), Mt 11:23 27:8; as subst., τὸ σ., He 3:13; id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμέραν, σ., He 4:7 R, mg., (v. Westc., in l.).

title: σήπω
content:
σήπω [in LXX; Ps 37 (38):5 (מקק ni.), Jb 33:21 (כּלה) 40:7, Si 14:19, al. ;]

to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (v. M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, Ja 5:2.†

title: σηρικός
content: σηρικός, v.s. σιρικός.

title: σής
content:
σής, σητός (late gen. for cl. σεός), ὁ, [in LXX: Jb 4:19, Is 50:9 (עָשׁ), Is 51:8 (סָס), al. ;]

a moth, clothes moth: Mt 6:19, 20, Lk 12:33.†

title: σητόβρωτος
content:
† σητό-βρωτος, -ον (< σής, βιβρώσκω), [in LXX: Jb 13:28 (אֲכָלוֺ עָשׁ) * ;]

moth-eaten: Ja 5:2.†

title: σθενόω
content:
*† σθενόω, -ῶ (< σθένος, strength),

to strengthen: c. acc., I Pe 5:10 (Hesych.).†

title: σιαγών
content:
σιαγών, -όνος, ἡ [in LXX for לְחִי ;]

the jawbone, jaw, cheek: Mt 5:39, Lk 6:29 (cf. MM, xxii).†

title: σιγάω
content:
σιγάω, -ῶ (< σιγή), [in LXX for חרשׁ, חשׁה, etc. ;]

1. intrans., to be silent, keep silence: Lk 9:36 18:39 20:26, Ac 12:17 15:12, 13, I Co 14:28, 30, 34.
2. Trans., to keep secret; pass., to be kept secret: Ro 16:25.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιωπάω

title: σιγή
content:
** σιγή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Wi 18:14, III Mac 3:23 * ;]

silence: Ac 21:40, Re 8:1.†

title: σιδήρεος
content:
σιδήρεος, -α, -ον (-οῦς, -ᾶ -οῦν) (< σίδηρος), [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]

of iron: Ac 12:10, Re 2:27 9:9 12:5 19:15.†

title: σίδηρος
content:
σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]

iron: Re 18:12.†

title: Σιδών
content:
Σιδών, -ῶνος, ἡ (Heb. צִידוֹן),

Sidon, a maritime city of Phœnicia: Mt 11:21, 22 15:21, Mk 3:8 7:24, 31, Lk 6:17 10:13, 14, Ac 27:3.†

title: Σιδώνιος
content:
Σιδώνιος, -α, -ον (< Σιδών),

of Sidon, Sidonian;
(a) the region: sc. χώρα, Lk 4:26;
(b) the people: Ac 12:20.†

title: σικάριος
content:
*† σικάριος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.; < sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii),

a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Ac 21:38.†

title: σίκερα
content:
† σίκερα, τό indecl. (Aram. שִׁכְרָא), [in LXX for שֵׁכָר (also rendered μέθυσμα, Jg 13:4, Mi 2:11), Le 10:9, al. ;]

fermented liquor, strong drink: Lk 1:15.†

title: Σίλας
content:
Σίλας, -α (acc to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; v. Dalman, Gr., 1575),

Silas (called also Σιλουανός, q.v.): Ac 15:22, 27, 32, 34, 40 16:19, 25, 29 17:4, 10, 14, 15 18:5 †

title: Σιλουανός
content:
Σιλουανός (in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form freq. in π.), -οῦ, ὁ,

Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: II Co 1:19, I Th 1:1, II Th 1:1, I Pe 5:12.†

title: Σιλωάμ
content:
Σιλωάμ (indecl., but in FlJ, gen., ᾶ, B.J., ii, 16, 2), ὁ (Heb. שִׁלֹחַ),

Siloam (v. DB, iii, 515 f.): Lk 13:4, Jo 9:7, 11.†

title: σιμικίνθιον
content:
*† σιμικίνθιον (also written σημι-), -ου, τό (Lat. semicinctium),

a work­man's apron: Ac 19:12.†

title: Σίμων
content:
Σίμων, -ωνος, ὁ

a Greek name (transliterated סִימוֺן in Heb.) used as a substitute for Συμεών (q.v.), Simon
1. Simon Peter: Mt 17:25, Mk 1:29, al.
2. Simon the Zealot (v.s. ζηλωτής, Καναναῖος): Mt 10:4, Mk 3:18, Lk 6:15, Ac 1:13.
3. One of the Brethren of our Lord (v.s. ἀδελψός): Mt 13:55, Mk 6:3.
4. The father of Judas Iscariot, himself surnamed Ἰσκαριώτης (q.v.): Jo 6:71 12:4 (Rec.) 13:2, 26
5. Simon the Cyrenian: Mt 27:32, Mk 15:21, Lk 23:26.
6. Simon the Pharisee: Lk 7:40, 43, 44.
7. Simon of Bethany, surnamed ὁ λεπρός: Mt 26:6, Mk 14:3.
8. Simon Magus, a Samaritan sorcerer: Ac 8:9, 13, 18, 24.
9. Simon the tanner, of Joppa: Ac 9:43 10:6, 17, 32.

title: Σινά
content:
Σινά (-ᾶ, Rec.),

indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό

(Heb. סִינַי),

Sinai (Ex 19:11, al.): Ac 7:30, 38, Ga 4:24, 25.†

title: σίναπι
content:
† σίναπι, -εως, τό (prob. Egyptian), = Attic τὸ νᾶπυ

mustard: Mt 13:31 17:20, Mk 4:31, Lk 13:19 17:6.†

title: σινδών
content:
σινδών, -όνος, ἡ [in LXX: Jg 14:12, 13A, Pr 31:24 (סָדִין), I Mac 10:64 A * ;]

fine linen cloth;
(a) as used for swathing dead bodies (cf. Hdt., ii, 86): Mt 27:59, Mk 15:46, Lk 23:53;
(b) a garment or wrap of this material (cf. ICC, Jg, l.c.): Mk 14:51, 52.†

title: σινιάζω
content:
*† σινιάζω (< σίνιον, a sieve), = σήθω,

to sift, winnow: fig., Lk 22:31.†

title: σιρικός
content:
* σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; v. Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν (< οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk),

silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Re 18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†

title: σιρός
content: σιρός, v.s. σειρός.

title: σιτευτός
content:
σιτευτός, -ή, -όν (< σιτεύω, to feed, fatten), [in LXX: III Ki 4:23 (אָבַס), etc. ;]

fattened: Lk 15:23, 27, 30.†

title: σιτίον
content:
σιτίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of σῖτος), [in LXX: Pr 24:57 (30:22) (לֶחֶם) *;]

1. corn, grain: Ac 7:12 (but v. Bl., §9, 1).
2. Mostly in pl., σιτία, bread, food, provisions (LXX, l.c., Hdt., al.).†

title: σιτιστός
content:
**† σιτιστός, -ή, -όν (< σιτίζω, to fatten) [in Sm.: Ps 21 (22):13, Je 46 (26):21 * ;]

= σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: Mt 22:4.†

title: σιτομέτριον
content:
*† σιτομέτριον, -ου, τό (< σιτομετρέω, Ge 47:12, 14 *, = Attic τὸν σῖτον μετρέω),

a measured portion of food: Lk 12:42 (for exx. in π., v. Deiss., BS, 158; LAE, 1031).†

title: σῖτος
content:
σῖτος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for דָּגָן ;]

wheat, corn: Mt 3:12 13:25, 29, 30 Mk 4:28, Lk 3:17 12:18 16:7 22:31, Jo 12:24, Ac 27:38, I Co 15:37, Re 6:6 18:13.†

title: Σιχάρ
content: Σιχάρ, v.s. Συχάρ.

title: Σιών
content:
Σιών

indecl.,
in NT anarth., but in LXX when used of the city of Jerusalem, ἡ Σ.

(Heb. צִיּוֹן),

Zion;
1. the mountain: in typical sense, of the Church, He 12:22; of heaven, Re 14:1.
2. The city, i.e. Jerusalem; in poetical sense;
(a) of the inhabitants: θυγάτηρ Σ, Mt 21:5, Jo 12:15 (LXX);
(b) in wider sense, of Israel: Ro 11:26;
(c) fig.: τίθήμι ἐν Σ λίθον, Ro 9:33, I Pe 2:6 (LXX).†

title: σιωπάω
content:
σιωπάω, -ῶ (< σιωπή, silence) [in LXX for חשׁה, חרשׁ hi., etc. ;]

to be silent or still, keep silence: Mt 20:31 26:63, Mk 3:4 9:34 10:48 14:61, Lk 19:4 , Ac 18:9; of one dumb, Lk 1:20 (cf. IV Mac 10:18); addressed rhetorically to the sea, σιώπα, Mk 4:39.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιγάω (q.v.).

title: σκανδαλίζω
content:
† σκανδαλίζω (< σκάνδαλον), [in LXX: Da LXX 11:41 (כּשׁל ni.), Si 9:5 35 (32):15 (יקשׁ ho.) ib. 23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Ps Sol 16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)* ;]

prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaph. of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: c. acc. pers., Mt 5:29, 30 17:27 18:6, 8, 9 Mk 9:42, 43, 45, 47 Lk 17:2, Jo 6:61, I Co 8:13. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: Mt 11:6 13:21, 57 15:12 24:10 26:31, 33, Mk 4:17 6:3 14:27, 29, Lk 7:23, Jo 16:1, Ro 14:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), II Co 11:29,†

title: σκάνδαλον
content:
† σκάνδαλον, -ου, τό (late form of the rare word σκανδάληθρον, v. LS, s.v.) [in LXX chiefly for מוֹקֵשׁ, מִכְשׁוֹל ;]

prop., the bait-stick of a trap, a snare, stumbling-block (Le 19:14, Jth 5:1): fig., Ro 9:33, I Pe 2:8 (Is 8:14; aliter in LXX; στερεὸν σκανδάλου in Aq.). Metaph., of that which causes error or sin;
(a) of persons: Mt 13:41 16:23; Χριστὸς ἐσταυρωμένος, I Co 1:23;
(b) of things: Mt 18:7, Ro 11:9 (LXX) 14:13, I Jo 2:10 Re 2:14; τὸ σ. τοῦ σταυροῦ, Ga 5:11; pl., Mt 18:7, Lk 17:1, Ro 16:17.†
SYN.: πρόσκομμα

title: σκάπτω
content:
σκάπτω [in LXX: Is 5:6 (עדר ni.)* ;]

to dig: Lk 6:48 13:8 16:3.†

title: σκάφη
content:
** σκάφη, -ης, ἡ (< σκάπτω), [in LXX: Da LXX Bel 32, TH ib. 33 * ;]

anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Ac 27:16, 30, 32.†

title: σκέλος
content:
σκέλος, -ους, τό [in LXX for רֶגֶל, etc. ;]

the leg from the hip downwards: Jo 19:31–33 †

title: σκέπασμα
content:
* σκέπασμα, -τος, τό (< σκεπάζω, to cover),

a covering, esp. clothing: I Ti 6:8.†

title: Σκευᾶς
content:
Σκευᾶς, -ᾶ

Sceva: Ac 19:14.†

title: σκευή
content:
** σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: III Mac 5:45 R * ;]

equipment, tackle: Ac 27:19.†

title: σκεῦος
content:
σκεῦος, -ους, τό [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;]

a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, v. MM, xxii): Mk 11:16, Lk 8:16, Jo 19:29, Ac 10:11, 16 11:5, Ro 9:21, Re 18:12; pl., II Ti 2:20, Re 2:27; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, He 9:21; pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, Mt 12:29, Mk 3:27, Lk 17:31; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., Ac 27:17. Metaph., of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, Ac 9:15; ὀργῆς, Ro 9:22; ἐλέους, ib. 23; σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. Ro 9:21), II Ti 2:21; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., I Pe 3:7; so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., I Th 4:4 (but v. infr.); of the body, II Co 4:7; so perh. I Th 4:4 (but v. supr., and v.s. κτάομαι).†

title: σκηνή
content:
σκηνή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל, also for מִשְׁכָּן, סֻכָּה, etc. ;]

a tent, booth, tabernacle: Mt 17:4, Mk 9:5, Lk 9:33, He 11:9; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., Lk 16:9; of the Mosaic tabernacle, He 8:5 9:2, 3, 6, 8, 21; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, Ac 7:44; of its heavenly prototype, He 8:2 9:11, Re 13:6 15:5 21:3; of the temple, He 13:10; ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, Ac 7:43 (LXX); metaph., ἡ σ. Δαυείδ Ac 15:16 (LXX).†

title: σκηνοπηγία
content:
σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ (< σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכּוֺת, De 16:16 31:10, Za 14:16, 18, 19; I Es 5:51, I Mac 10:21, II Mac 1:9, 18 * ;]

prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, Le 23:34, al.; v. Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: Jo 7:2.†

title: σκηνοποιός
content:
*† σκηνοποιός, -όν (< σκηνή, ποιέω),

making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Ac 18:3.†

title: σκῆνος
content:
** σκῆνος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Wi 9:15 * ;]

= σκηνή,
a tent, tabernacle (C.I., 3071). Metaph., of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: II Co 5:1, 4.†

title: σκηνόω
content:
σκηνόω, -ῶ (< σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכֵן ;]

to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, v. MM, Exp., xxii): seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Re 7:15; seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., Jo 1:14; id. c. dat. loc., Re 12:12 13:6; seq. μετά, c. gen. pers., Re 21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).†

title: σκήνωμα
content:
σκήνωμα, -τος, τό (< σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;]

a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Ps 131 (132):5, al.), Ac 7:46. Metaph., of the body: II Pe 1:13, 14.†

title: σκιά
content:
σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for צֵל, IV Ki 20:9 ff., Ps 56 (57):1, al.; but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, Jb 3:5, Ps 22 (23):4, Is 9:2 (1) (v. ICC, in l.), al. ;]

1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: Mk 4:32, Ac 5:15; metaph., σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, Mt 4:16, Lk 1:79 (LXX).
2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: fig., ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., He 8:5; opp. to σῶμα, Col 2:17; opp. to εἰκών, He 10:1.†

title: σκιρτάω
content:
σκιρτάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ge 25:22 (רצץ hithpo.), Ps 113 (114):4, 6 (רקד), etc. ;]

to leap: Lk 1:41, 44 6:23.†

title: σκληροκαρδία
content:
† σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ (< σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: De 10:16, Je 4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Si 16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, ib. 3:26, 27) * ;]

hardness of heart: Mt 19:8, Mk 10:5 16:[14].†

title: σκληρός
content:
σκληρός, -ά, -όν (< σκέλλω, to dry), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה ;]

hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opp. to μαλακός); metaph., in various uses;
(a) of men, hard, stern, severe: Mt 25:24;
(b) of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), Ac 26:14; λόγος, Jo 6:60; ἄνεμος, Ja 3:4; σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.†
SYN.: αὐστηρός, q.v

title: σκληρότης
content:
σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ (< σκληρός), [in LXX: De 9:27 (קְשִׁי), etc. ;]

hardness; metaph., of stubbornness: Ro 2:5.†

title: σκληροτράχηλος
content:
† σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον (σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: Ex 33:3, 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;]

stiff-necked: metaph., Ac 7:51.†

title: σκληρύνω
content:
σκληρύνω (< σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קשׁה hi., also for חזק ;]

to harden. Metaph., to harden, make stubborn: c. acc. pers., Ro 9:18; τ. καρδίας (Ps 94 (95):8), He 3:8, 15 4:7. Pass., to become hardened: Ac 19:9, He 3:13.†

title: σκολιός
content:
σκολιός, -ά, -όν [in LXX: De 32:5 (עִקֵּשׁ), Pr 28:18 (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דְּרָכַיׅם נֶעֱקַשׁ), Is 40:4 (עָקֹב), etc. ;]

curved, bent, winding (opp. to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): Lk 3:5 (LXX). Metaph., crooked, perverse, unjust: Ac 2:40, Phl 2:15, I Pe 2:18.†

title: σκόλοψ
content:
σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ [in LXX: Nu 33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Ho 2:6 (8) (סִיר), Ez 28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Si 43:19 * ;]

anything pointed, esp.
1. in cl., a stake
2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. c.): σ. τῇ σαρκί, II Co 12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†

title: σκοπέω
content:
** ακοπέω, -ῶ (< σκοπός), [in LXX: Es 8:13, II Mac 4:5 * ;]

to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaph., to look to, consider: c. acc. rei, II Co 4:13, Phl 2:4; c. acc. pers., Ro 16:17, Phl 3:17; seq. μή, Lk 11:35; σεαυτόν, seq. μή (v. M, Pr., 192), Ga 6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).†
SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω

title: σκοπός
content:
σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for צֹפֶה ;]

1. a watcher, watchman (Ez 3:17, al.).
2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wi 5:12, 21, al.). Metaph., of an aim or object: Phl 3:14.†

title: σκορπίζω
content:
σκορπίζω [in LXX for פּוּץ hi., etc. ;]

in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (v. MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, Jo 10:12; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, Mt 12:30, Lk 11:23; pass., seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Jo 16:32; of one who dispenses blessings, II Co 9:9 (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).†

title: σκορπίος
content:
σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for עַקְרָב ;]

a scorpion: Lk 10:19 11:12, Re 9:3, 5, 10.†

title: σκοτεινός
content:
σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν (< σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;]

dark: opp. to φωτεινός, Mt 6:23, Lk 11:34, 36.†

title: σκοτία
content:
† σκοτία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Jb 28:3 (אֹפֶל), Mi 3:6 (חָשְׁכָה), Is 16:3 * ;]

in late writers = σκότος,
darkness: Jo 6:17 20:1. Metaph.,
(a) of secrecy (opp. to ἐν τ. φωτί): Mt 10:27, Lk 12:3;
(b) of spiritual darkness: Mt 4:16, Jo 1:5 8:12 12:35, 46, I Jo 1:5 2:8, 9, 11.†

title: σκοτίζω
content:
† σκοτίζω (< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ ;]

to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Mt 24:29, Mk 13:24, Lk 23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Re 8:12. Metaph., of the mind, Ro 1:21 11:10 (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).†

title: σκότος
content:
σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf. σ., τό),

darkness: He 12:18, Rec.†

title: II σκότος
content:
σκότος, -ους, τό, a form rare in cl. (cf. ὁ σ.) but freq. in LXX, [chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ ;]

darkness: Mt 27:45, Mk 15:33, Lk 22:53 23:44, Ac 2:20, II Co 4:6; τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σ., I Co 4:5; of blindness, Mt 6:23, Ac 13:11; by meton., of a dark place, Mt 8:12 22:13 25:30, II Pe 2:17, Ju 13. Metaph., of moral and spiritual darkness: Lk 11:35, Jo 3:19, Ac 26:18, II Co 6:14, Eph 6:12, Col 1:13, I Pe 2:9; by meton., of those who are in spiritual darkness, Eph 5:8; τ. ἔργα τοῦ σ., Ro 13:12, Eph 5:11; οκότους εἶναι, I Th 5:5; ἐν σ. εἶναι, ib. 4; οἱ ἐν σ., Lk 1:79, Ro 2:19; ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σ., Mt 4:16 (LXX) (WH. σκοτίᾳ); ἐν σ. περιπατεῖν, I Jo 1:6.†

title: σκοτόω
content:
σκοτόω, -ῶ (< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ, קדר, שׁחר ;]

to darken: Re 9:2 16:10. Metaph., of the mind : pass., Eph 4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).†

title: σκύβαλον
content:
**† σκύβαλον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Si 27:4 * ;]

refuse, esp. dung (v. MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Phl 3:8.†

title: Σκύθης
content:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ

Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col 3:11.†

title: σκυθρωπός
content:
σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν) (< σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), [in LXX: Ge 40:7 (רַע), etc. ;]

of a gloomy countenance: Mt 6:16, Lk 24:17.†

title: σκύλλω
content:
* σκύλλω

1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.).
2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: c. acc. pers., Mk 5:35, Lk 8:49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Mt 9:36; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Lk 7:6 (freq. in π.; v. MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).†

title: σκῦλον
content:
σκῦλον (Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;]

mostly in pl., σκῦλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Lk 11:22.†

title: σκωληκόβρωτος
content:
* σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον (< σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω),

eaten of worms: Ac 12:23 (cf. II Mac 9:9, and v. MM, xxiii) †

title: σκώληξ
content:
σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;]

a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaph., of fut. punishment, Mk 9:48 (LXX, Is 66:24; cf. Si 7:17, Jth 16:17).†

title: σμαράγδινος
content:
*† σμαράγδινος (< σμάραγδος, q.v.),

1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11).
2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Re 4:3 (for the construction, v. Swete, in l.; Zorell, s.v.).†

title: σμάραγδος
content:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ (and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Ex 28:9 (שֹׁהַם) 36:17 (39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Ez 28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;]

emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, s.v.; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Re 21:19.†

title: σμύρνα
content:
σμύρνα (in some MSS, ζμ-; v. Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מוֹר מֹר ;]

myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mt 2:11, Jo 19:39.†

title: Σμύρνα
content:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ

Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Re 1:11 2:8.†

title: Σμυρναῖος
content:
Σμυρναῖος, -α, -ον

of Smyrna: Re 2:8, Rec.†

title: σμυρνίζω
content:
*† σμυρνίζω (< σμύρνα),

1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79).
2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mk 15:23.†

title: Σόδομα
content:
Σόδομα, -ων, τά (Heb. סְדֹם),

Sodom (Ge 13:10, 12, al.): Mt 10:15 11:23, 24 Lk 10:12 17:29, Ro 9:29 (LXX), II Pe 2:6, Ju 7, Re 11:8.†

title: Σολομών
content:
Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has freq. -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Ac 3:11 5:12; in Ac 7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; v. B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה),

Solomon: Mt 1:6, 7 6:29 12:42, Lk 11:31 12:27, Jo 10:23, Ac 3:11 5:12 7:47.†

title: σορός
content:
σορός, -οῦ, ἡ [in LXX: Ge 50:26 (אָרוֹן), Jb 21:32 A * ;]

(a) a cinerary urn (Hom.);
(b) a coffin (Hdt., i, 68, 3, al.): Lk 7:14.†

title: σός
content:
σός, -ή, -όν

possess. prop. of second pers.,
thy, thine: Mt 7:3, al.; as subst., οἱ σοί, thy kinsfolk, friends, Mk 5:19; τὸ σόν, what is thine, Mt 20:14 25:25; τὰ σά, thy goods, Lk 6:30

title: σουδάριον
content:
*† σουδάριον, -ου, τό (Lat.),

handkerchief, kerchief: Lk 19:20, Ac 19:12; used as a head covering for the dead, Jo 11:44 20:7 (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).†

title: Σουσάννα
content:
Σουσάννα, -ης (cf. Da LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.), ἡ,

Susanna: Lk 8:3.†

title: σοφία
content:
σοφία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חׇכְמָה ;]

skill, intelligence, wisdom, ranging from knowledge of the arts and matters of daily life to mental excellence in its highest and fullest sense;
(a) of human wisdom: I Co 2:1, 4, 5, Ja 3:15, Re 13:18 17:9; σ. Σολομῶνος, Mt 12:42, Lk 11:31; Αἰγυπτίων, Ac 7:22; Ἕλληνες σ. ζητοῦσιν, I Co 1:22; σ. λόγου, I Co 1:17; τ. σοφῶν, ib. 19 (LXX); τ. κόσμου, ib. 20, 21 3:19; ἀνθρωπίνη, I Co 2:13; σαρκική, II Co 1:12;
of wisdom in spiritual things: Lk 21:15, Ac 6:3, 10 7:10, I Co 2:6, Col 1:28 2:23 3:16 4:5, Ja 1:5 3:13, 17, II Pe 3:15; λόγος σοφίας, I Co 12:8; πνεῦμα σοφίας, Eph 1:17; σ. καὶ φρόνησις, Eph 1:8; σ. καὶ σύνεσις, Col 1:9;
(b) of divine wisdom: of God, Ro 11:33, I Co 1:21, 24 2:7, Re 7:12; πολυποίκιλος, Eph 3:10
of Christ, Mt 13:54, Mk 6:2, Lk 2:40, 52, I Co 1:30 Col 2:3, Re 5:12;
of wisdom personified, Mt 11:19, Lk 7:35 11:49.†
SYN.: σύνεσις, intelligence; φρόνησις, prudence, which with σ. make up (Arist., N. Eth., i, 13) the three intellectual ἀρεταί. σ. is wisdom primary and absolute; in distinction from which φ. is practical, σύνεσις critical, both being applications of σ. in detail (cf. Lft., and ICC on Col 1:9; Lft., Notes, 317 f.; Tr., Syn., § lxxv; Cremer, 870 ff.).

title: σοφίζω
content:
σοφίζω (< σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חכם ;]

to make wise, instruct: c. acc. pers., II Ti 3:15 (cf. Ps 18 (19):8 (Ps 118 (119):98). As depon., -ομαι;
(a) intrans., to become wise (III Ki 4:27 ( 5:11)), Ec 2:15, and freq. in Si 7:5, al.);
(b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., II Pe 1:16 (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).†

title: σοφός
content:
σοφός, -ή, -όν [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;]

skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: Ro 16:19, I Co 3:10; of the learned, Ro 1:14, 22, I Co 1:19, 20, 26, 27 3:18–20; of Jewish teachers, Mt 11:25, Lk 10:21; Christian, Mt 23:34; of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, I Co 6:5, Eph 5:15, Ja 3:13; of God, Ro 16:27; compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, I Co 1:25.†
SYN.: συνετός, φρόνιμος (v.s. σοφία, SYN.)

title: Σπανία
content:
Σπανία, -ας, ἡ (= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (I Mac 8:3) or Σ. as here),

Spain: Ro 15:24, 28.†

title: σπαράσσω
content:
σπαράσσω [in LXX: II Ki 22:8 B (גּעשׁ hith.), Je 4:19 (המה) Da LXX 8:7 (שׁלךְ hi.), III Mac 4:6 * ;]

1. to tear, rend, mangle.
2. to convulse: Mk 1:26 (v. Swete, in l.) Mk 9:26, Lk 9:39 (cf. συν-σπαράσσω).†

title: σπαργανόω
content:
σπαργανόω, -ῶ (< σπάργανον, a swathing-band) [in LXX: Jb 38:9, Ez 16:4 (חתל pu.)* ;]

to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: Lk 2:7, 12 (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).†

title: σπαταλάω
content:
† σπαταλάω, -ῶ (< σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Si 27:13 *), [in LXX: Ez 16:49 (שׁקט hi.), Si 21:15 * ;]

to live riotously: I Ti 5:6, Ja 5:5 (Polyb.).†
SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (v. Tr., Syn., § liv)

title: σπάω
content:
σπάω [in LXX chiefly for שׁלף, ;]

in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157),
to draw: μάχαιραν, Mk 14:47, Ac 16:27,†

title: σπείρα
content:
** σπείρα, -ης (on this form of gen., v. M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186), [in LXX: Jth 14:11, II Mac 8:23 12:20, 22 * ;]

1. (= Lat. spira) anything or rolled up, a coil.
2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (v. Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): Mt 27:27, Mk 15:16, Jo 18:3, 12, Ac 10:1 21:31 27:1.†

title: σπείρω
content:
* σπείρω [in LXX chiefly for זרע ;]

to sow (seed): absol., Mt 6:26 13:3, 4, 18 25:24, 26, Mk 4:3, 4, Lk 8:5 12:24, Jo 4:36, II Co 9:10; c. acc. rei, Mt 13:24, 27, 37, 39, Mk 4:32, Lk 8:5, I Co 15:36, 37; seq. εἰς, Mt 13:22, Mk 4:18; ἐν, Mt 13:24, 31; ἐπί, c. gen., Mk 4:31; ἐπί, c. acc, Mt 13:20, 23, Mk 4:16, 20; παρά, c. acc., Mt 13:19. Metaph.: I Co 9:11 15:42–44, Ga 6:7, 8, Ja 3:18; in proverbial sayings, Mt 25:24, 26, Lk 19:21, 22, Jo 4:37, II Co 9:6, Ga 6:7; in interpretation of parables, Mt 13:19–23, Mk 4:14–20 †

title: σπεκουλάτωρ
content:
*† σπεκουλάτωρ, -ορος (Rec. -ωρος), ὁ (Lat. speculator),

1. prop., a spy or scout.
2. An executioner: Mk 6:27 (v. Swete, in l.).†

title: σπένδω
content:
σπένδω [in LXX chiefly for נסך hi. ;]

to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., fig., σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Phl 2:17 (v. Lft., in l.), II Ti 4:6 (for exx. from π., v. Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†

title: σπέρμα
content:
σπέρμα, -τος, τό (< σπείρω) [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;]

seed;
(a) of plants: Mt 13:24, 27 37, 38, II Co 9:10; pl., Mt 13:32, Mk 4:31, I Co 15:33; metaph., of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Is 1:9; cf. Wi 14:6; Plat., Tim., 23 c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Ro 9:29;
(b) of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, Le 15:16, al.): He 11:11; metaph., of the divine influence, I Jo 3:9; by meton. (as freq. in poets), seed, offspring, posterity: Mt 22:24, 25, Mk 12:19–22, Lk 1:55 20:28 (LXX) Jo 7:42 8:33, 37 Ac 3:25 7:5, 6 13:23, Ro 1:3 4:13, 18 9:7, 8 11:1, II Co 11:22, Ga 3:16, 19, II Ti 2:8, He 2:16 11:18; pl. (FlJ, Ant., viii, 7, 6; Plat., Leg., ix, 853 c; IV Mac 18:1; in Ga, l.c., contrasted with sing., v. Lft., in l; Milligan, NTD, 105 f.), Ga 3:16; of spiritual offspring, Ro 4:16, 18 9:8, Ga 3:29, Re 12:17.†

title: σπερμολόγος
content:
* σπερμολόγος, -ον (< σπέρμα, λέγω)

a seed picker;
(a) prop., of birds (Arist., Aristoph, al.);
(b) in Attic slang, of an idler who lives on scraps picked up in the agora; hence, as subst., ὁ σ., an idle babbler: Ac 17:18.†

title: σπεύδω
content:
σπεύδω [in LXX chiefly for מהר pi., also for בּהל pi., hi., etc. ;]

1. most freq. intrans., to hasten: c. inf. (as freq. in cl.), Ac 20:16; ptcp. c. indic., Lk 2:16; c. imperat., Lk 19:5, 6; σπεῦσον κ. ἔξελθε, Ac 22:18
2. Trans., c. acc;
(a) to hasten, urge on, accelerate (as Hom., Od., xix, 137; Eur., Med., 152; Si 33(36):8): II Pe 3:12, R, mg. (cf. Mayor and ICC, in l., but v. infr.);
(b) to desire eagerly (Pind., Pyth., iii, 110; Eur., Suppl., 161; Is 16:5): II Pe, l.c., R, txt. (but v. supr.).†

title: σπήλαιον
content:
σπήλαιον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה ;]

a cave, cavern: Jo 11:38, He 11:38, He 6:15; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν (Je 7:11), Mt 21:13, Mk 11:17, Lk 19:46.†

title: σπιλάς
content:
* σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ (on the gender in Ju, l.c., v. Mayor, Ju., 41),

1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaph., of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but v. infr.).
2. In late writers = σπίλος (q.v.), a spot, stain; metaph., Ju, l.c., R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but v. supr.).†

title: σπίλος
content:
* σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ

1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.).
2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaph.,
(a) of moral blemish: Eph 5:27
(b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l.): II Pe 2:13.†

title: σπιλόω
content:
**† σπιλόω [in LXX: Wi 15:4 * ;]

to stain, spot, defile: c. acc., Ja 3:6, Ju 23.†

title: σπλαγχνίζομαι
content:
σπλαγχνίζομαι (< σπλάγχνον), [in LXX (act., -ίζω): Pr 17:5 A, II Mac 6:8 (= -εύω) * ;]

to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (q.v.), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., Lk 10:33 15:20; ptcp., σλαγχνισθείς, c. indic., Mt 18:27 20:34, Mk 1:41; seq. ἐπίπ, c. dat. pers., Mt 14:14, Lk 7:13; ἐπί, c. acc., Mt 15:32, Mk 6:34 8:2 9:22; περί, Mt 9:36. (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: I Ki 23:21, Ez 24:21, Test. Zeb., 4:6–7; v. Thayer, s.v.; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on Phl 1:8, in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) †

title: σπλάγχνον
content:
σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, [in LXX: Pr 12:10 (רַחֲמׅים, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, Ps 24 (25):6 39 (40):12 and by ἔλεος, Is 47:6), Pr 26:22 (בֶּטֶן), Wi 10:5, Si 30:7, II Mac 9:5, 6, al. ;]

the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): Ac 1:18. Metaph., of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; v. MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on Phl 1:8): II Co 6:12 7:15, Phm 7, 12, 20, I Jo 3:17; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, Col 3:12; σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, Phl 2:1; σ. ἐλέους θεοῦ; ἡμῶν, Lk 1:78; σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Phl 1:8.†

title: σπόγγος
content:
* σπόγγος, -ου, ὁ

a sponge: Mt 27:48, Mk 15:36, Jo 19:29.†

title: σποδός
content:
σποδός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for אֵפֶר ;]

ashes: He 9:13; ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ. (Is 58:5, Jo 3:6, Da LXX 9:3, al.), Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13.†

title: σπορά
content:
σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< σπείρω), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:29 (זרע), I Mac 10:30 * ;]

1. a sowing.
2. seedtime.
3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): I Pe 1:23
(cf. σπέρμα, and v. Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).†

title: σπόριμος
content:
σπόριμος, -ον (< σπείρω) [in LXX: Ge 1:29, Le 11:37 (זרע), Si 40:22 א1 * ;]

fit for sowing, sown; as subst., τὰ σ., corn-fields: Mt 12:1, Mk 2:23, Lk 6:1.†

title: σπόρος
content:
σπόρος, -ου, ὁ (< σπείρω), [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;]

= σπορά,
1. sowing or seedtime.
2. seed sown (so usually in late Gk.): Mk 4:26, 27, Lk 8:5, 11, II Co 9:10 a (LTr.); metaph., of almsgiving, II Co 9:10b .†

title: σπουδάζω
content:
σπουδάζω (< σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בּהלni.;]

to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: c. inf. (v. M, Pr., 205 f.), Ga 2:10, Eph 4:3, I Th 2:17, II Ti 2:15 4:9, 21, Tit 3:12, He 4:11, II Pe 1:10 3:14; c. acc. et inf. (on this construction v. Mayor in l.; MM, xxiii), II Pe 1:15 (for other constructions v. LS, s.v.).†

title: σπουδαῖος
content:
σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον (< σπουδή), [in LXX: Ez 41:25 * ;]

in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: seq. ἐν, II Co 8:22; compar., -οτεροσς ib. 17 (here in superl. sense, v. Bl., § 44, 3) 22.†

title: σπουδαίως
content:
** σπουδαίως adv. (< σπουδαῖος), [in LXX: Wi 2:6 * ;]

1. with haste or zeal, i.e. earnestly, zealously, diligently: Lk 7:4, II Ti 1:17, Tit 3:13; compar., -οτέρως, Phl 2:28 (RV, Lft., Weymouth, al., but v. infr.)
2. hastily, speedily: compar., -οτέρως, Phl 2:28 (Thayer, Zorell, s.v.; ICC, in l., al., but v. supr.).†

title: σπουδή
content:
σπουδή, -ῆς, ἡ (< σπεύδω), [in LXX chiefly for בּהל, its parts and derivatives ;]

1. haste, speed: μετὰ σ. (Wi 19:2), Mk 6:25, Lk 1:39.
2. zeal, diligence, earnestness: Ro 12:11, II Co 7:11, 12 8:7, 8; ἐν σ., Ro 12:8 (v. M, Pr, 104); seq. ὑπέρ, II Co 8:16; σπουδὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι, He 6:11; σ. παρεισφέρειν, II Pe 1:5; πᾶσαν σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Ju 3 (v. MM, xxiii; M, Pr., 214; Deiss., BS, 361, 364).†

title: σπυρίς
content: σπυρίς, v.s. σφυρίς.

title: στάδιον
content:
στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jo 6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (v. B1., § 9, 1), [in LXX: Da LXX 4:9, Su 37, II Mac 11:5 12:9 ff. * ;]

a stadium, i.e.
1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Mt 14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Lk 24:13, Jo 6:19 11:18, Re 14:20 21:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course,
2. a race-course: I Co 9:24.†

title: στάμνος
content:
στάμνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ [in LXX: Ex 16:33 (צִנְצֶנֶת), III Ki 12:24 14:3 (בַּקְבֻּק), Da LXX Bel 32 * ;]

prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: He 9:4.†

title: στασιαστής
content:
*† στασιαστής (< στασιάζω, to stir up sedition, Jth 7:15, II Mac 4:30 14:6 *)

= Att.. στασιώτης,
a rebel, revolutionist, one who stirs up sedition: Mk 15:7 (FlJ, al.).†

title: στάσις
content:
στάσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for עמד, its parts and derivatives, also for רִיב (Pr 17:14), etc. (v. Deiss., BS, 158 f.) ;]

1. a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν (Polyb., v, 5, 3; and cf. Lat. locum habere), He 9:8.
2. insurrection, sedition: Mk 15:7, Lk 23:19, 25, Ac 19:40 24:5.
3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension (cf. MM, xxiii) Ac 15:2 23:7, 10.†

title: στατήρ
content:
στατήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ [in Aq., Sm., for שֶׁקֶל ;]

a stater;
(a) a weight;
(b) a coin (used by late writers of the Greek τετράδραχμον): Mt 17:27 26:16, WH, mg.†

title: σταυρός
content:
* σταυρός, -οῦ, ὁ

1. an upright pale or stake (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.)
2. In late writers (Diod., Plut., al.) of the Roman instrument of crucifixion, the Cross: of the Cross on which Christ suffered, Mt 27:32, 40, 42, Mk 15:21, 30, 32, Lk 23:26, Jo 19:17, 19, 25, 31, Col 2:14, He 12:2; θάνατος σταυροῦ, Phl 2:8; τ. αἷμα τοῦ σ., Col 1:20. Metaph., in proverbial sayings: αἴρειν (λαμβάνειν, βαστάζειν) τὸν σ., Mt 10:38 16:24, Mk 8:34 10:21, 15:21, Lk 9:23 14:27 (for an interesting ex. of metaph. use in π., v. MM, xxiii) By meton., for Christ's death on the Cross: I Co 1:17, Ga 5:11 6:12, 14, Eph 2:16, Phl 3:18; ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σ., I Co 1:18.†

title: σταυρόω
content:
σταυρόω, -ῶ (< σταυρός), [in LXX: Es 7:9 (תּלה), Es 8:13 * ;]

1. to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.).
2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: c. acc. pers., Mt 20:19 23:34 26:2 27:22 ff. 28:5, Mk 15:16 ff. 16:6, Lk 23:21, 23, 33 24:7, 20, Jo 19:6 ff., Ac 2:36 4:10, I Co 1:13, 23 2:2, 8, II Co 13:4, Ga 3:1, Re 11:8; metaph., Ga 5:24 6:14.†

title: σταφυλή
content:
σταφυλή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX for עֵנָב ;]

a bunch of grapes: Mt 7:16, Lk 6:44, Re 14:18. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opp. to ὄμφαξ, cf. Ge 40:10, Jb 15:33; as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).†

title: στάχυς
content:
στάχυς, -υος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for שִׁבֹּלֶת ;]

an ear of corn: Mt 12:1, Mk 2:23 4:28, Lk 6:1.†

title: Στάχυς
content:
Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ

Stachys: Ro 16:9 (v. Lft., Phl., 174; MM, xxiii).†

title: στέγη
content:
στέγη, -ης, ἡ (< στέγω) [in LXX: Ge 8:13 (מִכְסֶה), etc. ;]

a roof: Mk 2:4; of entering a house, εἰσέρχεσθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σ., Mt 8:8, Lk 7:6 (cf. MM, xxiii).†

title: στέγω
content:
** στέγω (cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Si 8:17 * ;]

1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.).
2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Si, l.c., Polyb., al.): I Co 13:7, R, mg.
3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., v., Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): I Co 9:12 13:7, I Th 3:1, 5.†

title: στεῖρος
content:
στεῖρος, -ον also -α, -ον, [in LXX for עֲקֶרֶת, עֲקָרָה ;]

barren: of a woman, Lk 1:7, 36 23:29, Ga 4:27 (LXX).†

title: στέλλω
content:
στέλλω [in LXX (mid.): Ma 2:5 (חתת ni.), Pr 31:24 (26), Wi 7:14 14:1, II Mac 5:1, III Mac 1:19 4:11 * ;]

1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wi, II Mac, ll. c.).
2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: II Co 8:20; seq. ἀπό, II Th 3:6
(cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).†

title: στέμμα
content:
* στέμμα, -τος, τό (< στέφω, to put around, enwreath)

a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Ac 14:13.†

title: στεναγμός
content:
στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה, etc. ;]

a groaning: Ac 7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Ro 8:26.†

title: στενάζω
content:
στενάζω [in LXX for אנח ni., אנק, etc. ;]

to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Mk 7:34, II Co 5:2, 4, He 13:17, Ja 5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Ro 8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).†
SYN.: v.s. κλαίω

title: στενός
content:
στενός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for צַר, etc. ;]

narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii), Mt 7:13, 14, Lk 13:24.†

title: στενοχωρέω
content:
στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ (< στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Jos 17:15 (אוּץ), Jg 16:16 (אלץ pi.), Is 28:19 (20) (קצר) Is 49:19 (צרר), IV Mac 11:11 * ;]

1. to be straitened (cf. Is 49:19); metaph., to be anxious (Hipp., al.).
2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., II Co 4:8 6:12.†

title: στενοχωρία
content:
στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (v. supr.) [in LXX for צוּקָה, etc. ;]

narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaph. (Xen., Polyb., De 28:53, Wi 5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Ro 2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), II Co 6:4 12:10.†
SYN.: θλίψις, q.v

title: στερεός
content:
στερεός, -ά, -όν [in LXX: Nu 8:4 (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, Is 5:28 (צַר), etc. ;]

hard, firm, solid: τροψή, He 5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, fig., II Ti 2:19. Metaph.,
(a) in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.);
(b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, I Pe 5:9.†

title: στερεόω
content:
στερεόω, -ῶ (< στερεός), [in LXX: Is 42:5 (רקע), Je 5:3 (חזק pi.), etc. ;]

(a) to make firm or solid;
(b) to strengthen, make strong; c. acc. pers., Ac 3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., ib. 7. Metaph. (cf. Je, l.c.): τ. πίστει, pass., Ac 16:5.†

title: στερέωμα
content:
στερέωμα, -τος, τό (< στερεόω), [in LXX: Ge 1:6 ff., Ps 18 (19):1 150:1, Ez 1:22–26 10:1 13:5, Da LXX, TH 3:(56), 12:3 (רָקִיעַ), De 33:26 (שׁחק), Ps 17 (18):2 70 (71):3 (סֶלַע), Es 9:29, I Es 8:78 (82), Si 43:1, 8, I Mac 9:14 * ;]

a solid body;
(a) a support, foundation (Arist., al.); metaph., strength (Ps 17 70, I Mac, ll. c.); steadfastness, firmness: τ. πίστεως, Col 2:5;
(b) the dome of heaven (believed to be a solid canopy), the firmament (LXX).†

title: Στεφανᾶς
content:
Στεφανᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ

Stephanas: I Co 1:16 16:15, 17.†

title: Στέφανος
content:
Στέφανος, -ου, ὁ

Stephen: Ac 6:5, 8, 9 7:59 8:2 11:19 22:20.†

title: στέφανος
content:
στέφανος, -ου, ὁ (< στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה ;]

1. that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.).
2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, q.v.; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX for the golden crown of royalty (prop., διάδημα, q.v., cf. Hort and Mayor on Ja 1:12): Mt 27:29, Mk 15:17, Jo 19:2, 5, I Co 9:25, Re 4:4, 10 6:2 9:7 12:1 14:14. Metaph.: Phl 4:1, Re 3:11; τ. δικαιοσύνης (cf. Deiss., LAE, 312), II Ti 4:8; τ. δόξης, I Pe 5:4; καυχήσεως, I Th 2:19 (v. M, Th., in l.); τ. ζωῆς (gen. appos.), Ja 1:12, Re 2:10.†

title: στεφανόω
content:
στεφανόω, -ῶ (< στέφανος), [in LXX for עטר ;]

c. acc. pers.,
to crown: of a victor, II Ti 2:5. Metaph., δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, He 2:7, 9 (LXX).†

title: στῆθος
content:
στῆθος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Ex 28:23, 26 (29, 30) (לֵב), etc. ;]

the breast: Jo 13:25 21:10, Re 15:6; as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ., Lk 18:13 23:48,†

title: στήκω
content:
† στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (v. B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii), [in LXX: Ex 14:13 A, Jg 16:26 B, III Ki 8:11 B * ;]

= ἵστημι, to stand: Mk 3:31 11:25, Jo 1:26, Re 12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaph., to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Ga 5:1 (but v. Field, Notes, 189 f.), II Th 2:15; seq. ἐν, Jo 8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), I Co 16:13, Phl 1:27 4:1; c. dat., Ro 14:4.†

title: στηριγμός
content:
** στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Is 3:1 * ;]

1. a setting firmly, supporting.
2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: II Pe 3:17.†

title: στηρίζω
content:
στηρίζω [in LXX for סמך, שׂוּם (שׂים), etc. ;]

to fix, set fast, make fast: Lk 16:26; τ. πρόσωτον (Ez 6:2 13:17, al.; v. Dalman, Words, 30 f.), Lk 9:51. Metaph., to confirm, establish: c., acc., Lk 22:32, Ac 18:23, Ro 1:11 16:25, I Th 3:2, 13, II Th 3:3, Ja 5:8, I Pe 5:10, Re 3:2; id. seq. ἐν, II Th 2:17, II Pe 1:12.†

title: στιβάς
content:
** στιβάς, -άδος, ἡ, [in Aq.: Ez 46:23 (טִירוֺת) * ;]

a litter of leaves or rushes: pl., Mk 11:8 (Rec. στοιβ-).†

title: στίγμα
content:
στίγμα, -τος, τό (< στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Ca 1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;]

a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Ga 6:17 (v. Lft., in l.; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).†

title: στιγμή
content:
στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ (< στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Is 29:5 (פֶּתַע), II Mac 9:11 * ;]

a prick, a point; metaph., σ. χρόνου, a moment: Lk 4:5.†

title: στίλβω
content:
στίλβω [in LXX: Na 3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;]

to shine, glisten: Mk 9:3.†

title: στοά
content:
στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: Ez 40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;]

a portico: Jo 5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jo 10:23, Ac 3:11 5:12 †

title: στοιβάς
content: στοιβάς, v.s. στιβάς.

title: Στοϊκός
content: Στοϊκός, v.s. Στωικός.

title: στοιχεῖον
content:
** στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Wi 7:17 19:18, IV Mac 12:13 * ;]

prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence,
1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.).
2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.).
3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) He 5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Ga 4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, ib. 3, Col 2:8, 20 (but v. infr.).
4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. c.): II Pe 3:10, 12.
5. The heavenly bodies (Diog. Laert.).
6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. c., v. ICC on Col 2:8; Enc. Bibl., s.v. " Elements ").†

title: στοιχέω
content:
στοιχέω, -ῶ (< στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ec 11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;]

to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaph., in late writers, to walk by rule: Ac 21:24; c. dat., to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Ro 4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Ga 5:25 6:16, Phl 3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).†

title: στολή
content:
στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< στέλλω), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבֻשׁ, etc. ;]

1. an equipment, an armament (Æsch.).
2. Equipment in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jh 3:6, Es 8:15, I Mac 6:15): Mk 12:38 16:5, Lk 15:22 20:46, Re 6:11 7:9, 13, 14 22:14.†

title: στόμα
content:
στόμα, -τος, τό [in LXX chiefly for פֶּה ;]

the mouth: of man, Mt 15:11, Jo 19:29, Ac 11:8, al.; of animals, Mt 17:27, II Ti 4:17 (fig.), He 11:33, Ja 3:3, al.; fig., of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Re 12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. פִּי־חֶרֶב, Ge 34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Lk 21:24, He 11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opp. to καρδία, Mt 12:34, Ro 10:8, 10; in various phrases (some cl., some resembling Hebrew; cf. Bl., § 40, 9): ἀνοίγειν τ. σ. (v.s. ἀνοίγω); σ. πρὸς σ. (פֶּה אֵל־פֶּה, Nu 12:8; = cl., κατὰ σ., Hdt., al.), face to face, II Jo 12, III Jo 14; διὰ τοῦ σ. (of the Holy Spirit), Lk 1:70, Ac 1:16, al.; ἀπὸ (ἐκ) τοῦ σ. (cf. ἀπὸ σ. εἰπεῖν, Plat., al.), of speaking by word of mouth, Lk 22:71, Ac 22:14; δόλος (ψεῦδος) ἐν τ. σ., I Pe 2:22, Re 14:5 (LXX); metaph., ἡ ῥομφαία τοῦ σ., Re 2:16. By meton., for speech (Soph.): Mt 18:16 (LXX), Lk 19:22 21:15, II Co 13:1

title: στόμαχος
content:
* στόμαχος, -ου, ὁ (< στόμα),

prop., a mouth, an opening;
(a) in early Gk. writers, the throat;
(b) of the opening of the stomach (Arist.);
(c) in later writers (Plut., al.), the stomach: I Ti 5:23.†

title: στρατεία
content:
στρατεία (on the orthogr., v. Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ (< στρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]

an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaph., II Co 10:4 (-τιά, T), I Ti 1:18.†

title: στράτευμα
content:
** στράτευμα, -τος, τό (< στρατεύω), [in LXX: I Mac 9:34, II Mac 5:24 8:21 12:38 13:13; pl., Jth 11:8, IV Mac 5:1 * ;]

1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.).
2. an army, a host: pl., Mt 22:7, Re 9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Ac 23:10, 27; pl., Lk 23:11.†

title: στρατεύω
content:
στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT (< στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יצא, צבא; metaph., IV Mac 9:23 ;]

used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Lk 3:14, I Co 9:7, II Ti 2:4. Metaph. (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: II Co 10:3, I Ti 1:18, Ja 4:1, I Pe 2:11.†

title: στρατηγός
content:
στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (< στρατός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;]

1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.).
2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Ac 16:20, 22, 35, 36, 38.
3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Ac 4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Lk 22:4, 52.†
SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Ac 16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217).

title: στρατιά
content:
στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]

1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (III Ki 22:19, al.), Lk 2:13; of the stars of heaven (Je 8:2, II Ch 33:3), Ac 7:42.
2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: II Co 10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).†

title: στρατιώτης
content:
στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX; II Ki 23:8 B1, II Mac 5:12 14:39, III Mac 3:12 ; IV Mac3 * ;]

a soldier: Mt 8:9, Mk 15:16, Jo 19:2, Ac 10:7, al.; metaph., σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., II Ti 2:3.†

title: στρατολογέω
content:
*† στρατολογέω, -ῶ (< στρατός, λέγω),

to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: II Ti 2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).†

title: στρατοπεδάρχης
content: στρατοπεδάρχης, v.s. στρατοπέδαρχος

title: στρατοπέδαρχος
content: *† στρατοπέδ-αρχος (Rec. -ης), -ου, ὁ (< στρατόπεδον, ἄρχω), a military commander, esp. the Pretorian prefect: Ac 28:16 (WH, om.).†

title: στρατόπεδον
content:
στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό (στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Je 41 (34):1 (חַיִל), II Mac 8:12, al. ;]

(a) a military camp;
(b) an army: Lk 21:20.†

title: στρεβλόω
content:
στρεβλόω, -ῶ (< στρέφω), [in LXX: II Ki 22:27 (פּתל hithp.), III Mac 4:14, IV Mac 9:17 12:4, 11 15:14 * ;]

to twist, torture. Metaph. (cf. II Ki, l.c.), to twist or pervert language: II Pe 3:16.†

title: στρέφω
content:
στρέφω [in LXX chiefly for הפך, also for סבב, etc. ;]

to turn: c. acc. rei dat. pers., Mt 5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Mt 27:3 (cf. Is 38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Ac 7:42; c. acc. seq. εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Re 11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: seq. εἰς, Jo 20:14, Ac 7:39 13:46; ptcp., στραφείς, c. indic., Mt 7:6 9:22 16:23, Lk 7:9 9:55 14:25 22:61, Jo 1:38 20:16; id. seq. πρός, Lk 7:44 10:22 (WH, R, om.), ib. 23 23:28; metaph., to change: absol., Mt 18:3, Jo 12:40 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στρέφω).†

title: στρηνιάω
content:
** στρηνιάω, -ῶ (< στρῆνος, q.v.), [in Sm.: Is 61:6 (אכל) * ;]

a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Re 18:7, 9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (q.v.), τρυφάω

title: στρῆνος
content:
στρῆνος, -ους, τό (cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;]

insolent luxury, wantonness: Re 18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, v. Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†

title: στρουθίον
content:
στρουθίον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;]

dimin. of στρουθός
a sparrow: Mt 10:29, 31, Lk 12:6, 7.†

title: στρωννύω
content:
στρωννύω or στρώννυμι (v. Bl., § 23, 1; Veitch, s.v.), [in LXX for יצע hoph., etc. ;]

to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Mt 21:8, Mk 11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Ac 9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Ez 23:41), Mk 14:15, Lk 22:12.†

title: στυγητός
content:
* στυγητός, -όν (< στυγέω, to hate),

hated, hateful: Tit 3:3.†

title: στυγνάζω
content:
† στυγνάζω (< στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Is 5:17, Wi 17:5, Da LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Ez 27:35 28:19 32:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;]

to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mk 10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mt 16:3 (|[WH]|, R, mg., om.).†

title: στύλος
content:
στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc. ;]

a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Re 10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, fig., Re 3:12, Metaph., Ga 2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, I Ti 3:15.†

title: Στωικός
content:
Στωικός (Rec. -ϊκός, T, Στοϊκός), -ή, -όν,

Stoic: Ac 17:18.†

title: σύ
content:
σύ, pron. of 2nd pers.,

thou, you, gen., σοῦ, dat., σοί, acc., σέ, pl., ὑμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς (enclitic in oblique cases sing., except after prep. (BL, §48, 3), though πρὸς σέ occurs in Mt 25:39). Nom. for emphasis or contrast: Jo 1:30, 42 4:10 5:33, 39, 44, Ac 4:7, Eph 5:32; so also perhaps σὺ εἶπας, Mt 26:64, al. (M, Pr., 86); before voc., Mt 2:6, Lk 1:76, Jo 17:5, al.; sometimes without emphasis (M, Pr., 85f.), as also in cl., but esp. as rendering of Heb. phrase, e.g. υἱός μου εἶ σύ (בְּנִי־אַתָּה, Ps 2:7), Ac 13:33. The gen. (σοῦ, ὑμῶν) is sometimes placed bef. the noun: Lk 7:48, 12:30, al.; so also the enclitic σοῦ, Mt 9:6; on τί ἐμοὶ κ. σοί, v.s. ἐγώ.

title: συγγένεια
content:
συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ (< συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]

1. kinship.
2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Lk 1:61, Ac 7:3, 14 †

title: συγγενεύς
content: **† συγγενεύς, v.s. συγγενής.

title: συγγενής
content:
σνγγενής, -ές (dat. pl., -εῦσιν, Mk 6:4, Lk 2:44, as though from -εύς, v. Swete, Mk., l.c.; Bl., § 8, 6; cf. I Mac 10:89 Aא2 *;) (< σύν, γένος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, דּוֹדָה, מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]

1. congenital, natural, innate.
2. akin to; as subst., a kinsman: Mk 6:4, Lk 1:58 2:44 14:12 21:16, Jo 18:26, Ac 10:24; of tribal kinship, Ro 9:3 16:7, 11, 21.†
SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (q.v.)

title: συγγενίς
content:
*† συγγενίς, -ίδος, ἡ,

late fem. form of σνγγενής, q.v.,
a kinswoman: Lk 1:36.†

title: συγγνώμη
content: συγγνώμη, v.s. συνγνώμη.

title: συγκ-
content: συγκ-, v. passim συνκ-.

title: συγκυρία
content:
** συγκυρία, -ας, ἡ (< συγκυρέω, to happen), [in Sm.: I Ki 6:9 (מִקְרֶה) * ;] (more freq. in late writers, συγκύρησις, -ημα),

chance, coincidence: κατὰ σ. (v. MM, xxiii), Lk 10:31 (Hippocr., Eccl.).†

title: συγχ-
content: συγχ-, v. passim συνχ-.

title: σύγχυσις
content:
σύγχυσις, -εως, ἡ (< συγχέω), [in LXX: Ge 11:9 (בָּבֶל), I Ki 5:6, 12 (11) 14:20 (מְהוּמָה) * ;]

confusion: of a popular uproar, Ac 19:29.†

title: συζ-
content: συζ-, v. passim συνζ-.

title: συκάμινος
content:
συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.) ;]

the mulberry tree

(Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, I Mac 6:34 *),

the sycamine: Lk 17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (v.s. συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; v. ICC, in l.; DB, iv, 634.) †

title: συκῆ
content:
συκῆ (contr. fr. συκέα), -ῆς, ἡ (< σῦκον), [in LXX for תְּאֵנָה ;]

a fig-tree: Mt 21:19–21 24:32, Mk 11:13, 20, 21 13:28, Lk 13:6, 7 21:29, Jo 1:49, 51, Ja 3:12, Re 6:13.†

title: συκομορέα
content:
*† συκο-μορέα (Rec. -μωραία, L, -μωρέα), -ας, ἡ, more commonly (so Aq., Sm., Ps 77 (78):47, Is 9:10 (9)) συκόμορος (< σῦκον + μόρον, the black mulberry),

a fig-mulberry, a sycamore: Lk 19:4 (cf. συκάμινος).†

title: σῦκον
content:
σῦκον, -ου, τό [in LXX for תְּאֵנָה ]

a fig: Mt 7:16, Mk 11:13, Lk 6:44 Ja 3:12.†

title: συκοφαντέω
content:
συκοφαντέω, -ῶ (< σῦκον, φαίνω), [in LXX: Ge 43:18 (גּלל hithpo.), Le 19:11 (שׁקר pi.), Jb 35:9, Ps 118 (119):122, Pr 14:31 22:16 28:3, Ec 4:1 (עשׁק) *;]

to act the συκοφάντης (on conjectures as to the origin of the term, v. LS, s.v.), to accuse falsely (Aristoph., Xen., al.): Lk 3:14 (R, mg.) 19:8 (RV, exact wrongfully; but cf. Hatch, Essays, 89 ff., v. also Field, Notes, 56 f.; MM, xxiv).†

title: συλαγωγέω
content:
*† συλαγωγέω, -ῶ (< σύλη, booty + ἄγω),

to carry off as spoil, lead captive (θυγατέρα, Heliod., Aeth., 10, 35): metaph., Col 2:8.†

title: συλάω
content:
** συλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ep. Je 1:18 * ;]

c. acc. pers., to strip, plunder, spoil: II Co 11:8.†

title: συλλ-
content: συλλ-, v. passim συνλ-.

title: συλλαμβάνω
content:
συλ-λαμβάνω [in LXX for תּפשׂ, הרה, etc. ;]

1. c. acc., to bring together, collect.
2. to seize, take: c. acc. pers., as a prisoner, Mt 26:55, Mk 14:48, Lk 22:54, Jo 18:12, Ac 1:16 12:3; pass., Ac 23:27; mid., in sense of act., Ac 26:21; σ. ἄγραν ἰχθύων, Lk 5:9.
3. C. dat. pers., to take part with, assist, succour; mid., in same sense: Lk 5:7, Phl 4:3.
4. Of a woman, to conceive: absol., Lk 1:24; seq. ἐν γαστρί, Lk 1:31; c. acc., Lk 1:36; ib. seq. ἐν τ. κοιλίᾳ, Lk 2:21; metaph., of lust producing sin, Ja 1:15.†

title: συλλέγω
content:
συλ-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for לקט ;]

to bring together, collect, gather up: c. acc. rei, Mt 13:28–30; pass., ib. 40; c. acc., seq. ἀπό, Mt 7:16; id. seq. ἐκ, Mt 13:41, Lk 6:44; seq. εἰς, Mt 13:48.†

title: συλλογίζομαι
content:
συλ-λογίζομαι [in LXX chiefly for חשׁב pi. ;]

1. to compute.
2. to reason: Lk 20:5.†

title: συμβ-
content: συμβ-, v. passim συνβ-.

title: συμβαίνω
content:
συμ-βαίνω [in LXX for עשׂה, קרא, קרה, etc. ;]

1. to stand with the feet together.
2. to come together, come to terms.
3. Of events, to come to pass, happen: c. dat. pers., Mk 10:32, Ac 3:10 20:19, I Co 10:11, I Pe 4:12, II Pe 2:22; absol., τὰ συμβεβηκότα, Lk 24:14 (cf. I Mac 4:26); c. acc. et inf., Ac 21:35.†

title: συμβουλεύω
content:
συμ-βουλεύω [in LXX chiefly for יעץ ;]

1. to advise, counsel: c. dat. pers., Jo 18:14; id. seq. inf., Re 3:18.
2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: seq. ἵνα, Mt 26:4 ("reciprocal middle," v. M, Pr., 157); c. inf., Ac 9:23.†

title: συμβούλιον
content:
**† συμβούλιον, -ου, τό (< σύμβουλος), [in LXX: IV Mac 17:17 א * ;]

a word of the Græco-Roman period (of. Lat. consilium, and v. Deiss., BS, 238) = cl. συμβουλία (Arist., Xen.),
1. counsel: σ. λαμβάνειν, Mt 12:14 22:15 27:1, 7 28:12; διδόναι, Mk 3:6 (ποιεῖν, Rec.); ποιεῖν, Mk 15:1 (ἑτοιμάζειν, WH, mg.).
2. By meton., a council (IV Mac, l.c.א; συνέδριον, AR): Ac 25:12 (v. MM, xxiv).†

title: σύμβουλος
content:
σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ (< σύν, βουλή), [in LXX forיוֺעֵץand cogn. forms ;]

a counsellor, adviser: Ro 11:34 (LXX).†

title: Συμεών
content:
Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן),

Simeon (so always AV; RV in Lk 2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, q.v., was also used;
1. the son of Jacob (Ge 29:33): Re 7:7.
2. An ancestor of our Lord: Lk 3:30
3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Lk 2:25, 34.
4. One surnamed Niger: Ac 13:1.
5. The apostle Peter: Ac 15:14, II Pe 1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).†

title: συμμ-
content: συμμ-, v. passim συνμ-.

title: συμμορφίζω
content:
*† συμ-μορφίζω (T, συν-), (< σύμμορφος),

to conform to: pass. ptcp., Phl 3:10 (v. Lft., Phl., 128).†

title: σύμμορφος
content:
*† σύμ-μορφος, -ον (< σύν, μορφή),

1. absol., similar (Luc.).
2. con­formed to: c. dat., Phl 3:21; c. gen., Ro 8:29 (v. B1., § 36, 11; 37, 6).†

title: συμμορφόω
content:
συμ-μορφόω, -ῶ

Rec. for -ίζω (q.v.), Phl 3:10.†

title: συμπ-
content: συμπ-, v. passim συνπ-.

title: συμπαθής
content:
συμπαθής, -ές (< σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Jb 29:25 A (אֹבֵל), IV Mac 5:25א, 13:23 15:4 * ;]

1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: I Pe 3:8.
2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.c.; Dion. H.).†

title: συμπαραμένω
content:
συμ-παρα-μένω

Rec, for παρα-μένω (q.v.), Phl 1:25.†

title: συμπόσιον
content:
συμπόσιον, -ου, τό (< συμπίνω), [in LXX: Es 7:7 (מִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן) 4:17, I Mac 16:16, II Mac 2:27, III Mac 4:16 5:36 6:33; σ. οἴνου, Sir 34 (31):31 35 (32):5, 49:1 * ;]

1. a drinking party
2. By meton., of the party itself, the guests (Plut); pl., σ. σ. (colloq.; v. M, Pr., 97), in parties or companies: Mk 6:39.†

title: συμφ-
content: συμφ- v. passim συνφ-.

title: συμφέρω
content:
συμ-φέρω [in LXX: Je 33 (26):14 (טוֹב), Pr 19:10 (נָאוֶה), Si 30:19, al. ;]

1. trans. to bring together: c. acc. rei, Ac 19:19.
2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: I Co 6:12 10:23, II Co 8:10; c. inf. (M, Pr., 210), Mt 19:10, Jo 18:14; c. dat., seq. ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 5), Mt 5:29, 30 18:6, Jo 11:50 16:7. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: I Co 12:7; pl., Ac 20:20; (οὐ σ. sc. ἐστιν; = οὐ συμφέρει; cf. Thuc., iii, 44, 2), II Co 12:1; as subst., τὸ σ., profit, He 12:10.†

title: σύμφορος
content:
** σύμ-φορος, -ον (< συμφέρω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:5 * ;]

profitable, useful, expedient. As subst., τὸ σ. (in cl. usually pl., τὰ σ.), advantage, profit: c. gen. pers., I Co 7:35 10:33.†

title: συμφυλέτης
content:
*† συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ (< σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Za 13:7; and v. Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.)

a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: I Th 2:14 (v. M, Th., in l., and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.†

title: σύμφυτος
content:
σύμ-φυτος, -ον (< συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: Za 11:2 (בּצר), Es 7:7, 8א2, Am 9:13, III Mac 3:22 * ;]

1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; III Mac, l.c.).
2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (v. Field, Notes, 155 f.), Ro 6:5.†

title: συμφωνέω
content:
συμ-φωνέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Ge 14:3 (חבר) II Ki 12:8 (9) (אוֺת ni.), Is 7:2 (נוּחַ), IV Mac 14:6 * ;]

prop., to agree in sound, be in harmony (Plat., Arist.). Metaph.,
(a) to agree with, agree together: Lk 5:36; c. dat. rei, Ac 15:15; seq. περί, Mt 18:19; pass., c. dat. pers., συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν, Ac 5:9;
(b) to agree as to a price (Polyb., Diod.): c. dat. pers., gen. pret., Mt 20:13; seq. μετά … ἐκ, ib. 2.†

title: συμφώνησις
content:
*† συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ (< συμφωνέω),

concord, agreement: seq. πρός, c. acc. pers., II Co 6:15.†

title: συμφωνία
content:
συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ (< σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Da LXX TH 3:5, 15, TH ib. 7, 10 (סוּמפֹּנְיָה) IV Mac 14:3 A * ;]

1. symphony, music: Lk 15:25
2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. c.; v MM, xxiv).†

title: σύμφωνος
content:
σύμφωνος, -ον (< σύν, φωνή), [in LXX: Ec 7:15 (14) (לְעֻמַּת), IV Mac 7:7 14:7 * ;]

agreeing in sound. Metaph., harmonious, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου (for exx. from π., v. Deiss., BS, 255), by agreement, I Co 7:5.†

title: συμψ-
content: συμψ-, v. passim συνψ-.

title: συμψηφίζω
content:
συμ-ψηφίζω [in LXX: Je 29 (49):20 A * ;]

to reckon together, count up: Ac 19:19.†

title: σύν
content:
σύν (old Att. ξύν), prep. c. dat.,

expressing association, fellowship and inclusion. It gradually gave way to μετά, c. gen. (cf. LS, s.v.; Bl., § 41, 3), and is therefore comparatively infrequent in NT, being rare in Mt4, Mk6, Jo3, and elsewhere (exx. Ja 1:11, II Pe 1:18) only in Lk (Gosp. and Ac) and Paul. With, together with: of companionship and association, Lk 2:13, Jo 21:3, Ac 10:23, al.; εἶναι σύν τινι, Lk 7:12, Ac 4:13, Phl 1:23, al.; of partisanship, Ac 4:13; οἱ σύν τινι (ὄντες), of attendants, companions or colleagues, Mk 2:26, Lk 5:9, Ac 5:17, al.; of assistance, ἡ χάρις τ. θεοῦ σὺν ἐμοί, I Co 15:10; of two or more things together, almost = καί, Lk 23:11, Ac 3:4 10:2 14:5 23:15, Eph 3:18; σὺν Χριστῷ ζῆν, II Co 13:4; besides (FlJ, LXX), σὺν πᾶσι τούτοις, Lk 24:21.
In composition: with (συνχαίρω), together (συνωδίνω), altogether (συντελέω).

title: συνάγω
content:
συν-άγω [in LXX chiefly forאסף, also forקבץ, etc. (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 128) ;]

to gather or bring together: of things, Jo 6:12, 13; seq. εἰς, Mt 3:12, al.; ἐκεῖ, Lk 12:18; ποῦ, Lk 12:17; συναγαγὼν πάντα (sc. εἰς ἀργύριον; v. Field, Notes, 68, MM, xxiv), having sold off all: Lk 15:13; of persons, Jo 11:52; esp. of assemblies, Mt 2:4, Jo 11:47, Ac 14:27, al. Pass., to be gathered or come together: Mt 22:41, Mk 2:2, Lk 22:66, al.; seq. ἐπί Mk 5:21, Ac 4:27; πρός, Mt 13:2, Mk 4:1, al.; εἰς, Re 19:17; ἐν, Ac 11:26; μετά, Mt 28:12; οὗ, Mt 18:20; ὅπου, Mt 26:57; ἐκεῖ, Jo 18:2, al.
In late writers (v. Kennedy, Sources, 128; cf. De 22:2, al.), to receive hospitably, entertain: Mt 25:35, 38, 43 (cf. ἐπι-συνάγω)

title: συναγωγή
content:
συν-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for עֵדָה, also for קהל, etc. ;]

prop., a bringing together;
1. of things,
(a) a gathering in of harvest;
(b) a collection of money.
2. Of persons,
(a) a collecting, assembling (Polyb.);
(b) an assembly (MM, xxiv; Deiss., LAE, 101 ff.): Re 2:9 3:9; esp. of a Jewish religious assembly, a synagogue: Lk 12:11, Ac 9:2, al.; of a Christian assembly, Ja 2:2. By meton., of the building in which the assembly is held, a synagogue: Mt 10:17, Mk 1:21, al. (cf. Cremer, s.v. ἐκκλησία)
SYN.: ἐκκλησία (q.v.)

title: συναγωνίζομαι
content:
* συν-αγωνίζομαι

to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): c. dat. pers. et rei, Ro 15:30.†

title: συναθλέω
content:
* συν-αθλέω, -ῶ

= συναγωνίζομαι: c. dat. commod., Phl 1:27; c. dat. pers., seq. ἐν, Phl 4:3.†

title: συναθροίζω
content:
συν-αθροίζω [in LXX chiefly for קבץ ;]

to gather together, assemble: c. acc. pers., Ac 19:25; pass., Ac 12:12.†

title: συναίρω
content:
συν-αίρω [in LXX: Ex 23:5 (עזב) * ;]

to take up together: σ. λόγον (of which there are several exx. in π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 118 f.; MM, i, xxiv; M, Pr., 160), to settle accounts, Mt 18:23, 24; seq. μετά, C. gen. pers., Mt 25:19.†

title: συναιχμάλωτος
content:
*† συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ

a fellow prisoner (prop., of a captive in war, v. Lft., Col., 234): Ro 16:7, Col 4:10, Phm 23.†

title: συνακολουθέω
content:
** συν-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX: II Mac 2:4, 6 * ;]

to follow along with, accompany: c. dat. pers., Mk 14:51, Lk 23:49; seq. μετά, c. gen. pers., Mk 5:37.†

title: συναλίζω
content:
** συν-αλίζω [in Al.: Ps 140 (141):4 * ;]

to assemble with: Ac 1:4 (EV, mg., eating with, but on this rendering and on the force of the pres. ptcp. here, v. Field, Notes, 110).†

title: συναλλάσσω
content:
* συν-αλλάσσω,

to reconcile: impf. (conative, v. M, Pr., 129), Ac 7:26.†

title: συναναβαίνω
content:
συν-ανα-βαίνω [in LXX for עלה ;]

to go up with: c. dat. pers., seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Mk 15:41, Ac 13:31.†

title: συνανάκειμαι
content:
**† συν-ανά-κειμαι [in LXX: III Mac 5:39 * ;]

to recline with or together at table: Mt 14:9, Mk 6:22, Lk 7:49 14:15; c. dat. pers., Mt 9:10, Mk 2:15, Lk 14:10.†

title: συναναμίγνυμι
content:
* συν-ανα-μίγνυμι (acc to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), [in LXX: Ho 7:8 A (בּלל hithpo.), Ez 20:18 A * ;]

to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaph., to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): I Co 5:9, 11, II Th 3:14 (v. M, Th., 117).†

title: συναναπαύομαι
content:
συν-ανα-παύομαι [in LXX: Is 11:6 (רבץ) * ;]

c. dat. pers., to lie down to rest with, sleep with. Metaph., to be refreshed in spirit with: Ro 15:32 (L, om.).†

title: συναντάω
content:
συν-αντάω, -ῶ [in LXX for פּגע,פּגשׁ,קרא,קרה, etc. ;]

to meet with: c. dat. pers., Lk 9:18, 37 22:10, Ac 10:25, He 7:1, 10. Metaph., of events, to happen, befall (Diog. L., Plut., al.): Ac 20:22.†

title: συνάντησις
content:
συν-άντησις, -εως, ἡ

Rec. for ὑπάντησις (q.v.), Mt 8:34.†

title: συναντιλαμβάνομαι
content:
† συν-αντι-λαμβάνομαι [in LXX: Ge 30:8 R (†), Ex 18:22, Nu 11:17 (נשׂא), Ps 88 (89):21 (כּוּן ni.) * ;]

to take hold with at the side for assistance; hence, to take a share in, help in bearing, and generally, help (with various constructions, v. LXX, ll. c., Deiss., LAE, 83 f.): c. dat., Lk 10:40, Ro 8:26.†

title: συναπάγω
content:
συν-απ-άγω [in LXX: Ex 14:6 (לקח) * ;]

to lead away with or together (Ex, l.c.). Pass., metaph. (as συμπεριφέρομαι, v. LS, s.v.), to be carried away with: c. dat., Ga 2:13, II Pe 3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, v. ICC, in l.; Field, Notes, 163), Ro 12:16.†
